strategy.title: No plan: the whole counted shooting-range market is worth $34,000, below $60,000
strategy.why: The state registry lists 85 indoor ranges, each buying one workbook a year at $400: every range buying brings $34,000. $60,000 needs 150 sales. At the measured 18% conversion (9 of 50) the realistic take is about 15 sales, about $6,100.

alternatives.title: Sell the workbook to the 85 registry ranges anyway
alternatives.why: Sound economics ($400 price, $6 cost, 3-day settlement) but caps at $34,000 and realistically about $6,100.

alternatives.title: Find ranges in other states or other buyers
alternatives.why: Not counted on the record; would need research.

brain.summary: INFEASIBLE AS STATED: the openings held sell into markets research counted whole: every buyer in them agreeing at the top price brings at most $34,000, so they cannot reach the $60,000 still needed. To make it supportable, target: lower the target to about $34,000, the most the openings held bring with every buyer agreeing at the top price. The conclusion covers the openings held; markets nobody has counted are not ruled out, so Brain keeps searching for openings outside them.

facts.value: The state's shooting-range registry lists 85 indoor ranges; each buys one sampling-log workbook a year, for its annual exposure review.
Sell Airborne-lead and surface-sampling log workbook for indoor shooting ranges to each buyer.
Range owners and range safety officers at indoor shooting ranges
Nine ranges each paid $400 for the workbook on this seller's checkout (Oct-Nov 2026).

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN with decisive link MARKET_VOLUME and a TARGET constraint is correct and is a genuine constraint, not missing evidence: every link of the only opening is evidenced (price $400 from nine real purchases on this seller's checkout, conversion 9/50 measured on this offer, cost $6, 3-day settlement, Brain-proved spreadsheet fulfilment, $0 exposure), and the whole evidenced population - 85 registry ranges each buying once a year - brings at most 85 x $400 = $34,000 in 30 days, below $60,000 (150 sales needed). Brain's own check agrees (NOT_VIABLE, supported reach $34,000).
findings: Recomputed: 85 x $400 = $34,000 ceiling; $60,000 / $400 = 150 sales; 0.18 x 85 = 15.3 sales = about $6,120 realistic. Matches.

Ceiling may be lower than stated: the nine ranges that paid in Oct-Nov 2026 each buy once a year; if they are among the 85 registry ranges, only 76 can buy in the window (76 x $400 = $30,400). The target suggestion 'at most $34,000' should note this overlap; it does not change the stance.

Resolution (lower the target, or count other states' range registries for 65+ more buyers) names the decisive evidence correctly; 65 more buyers at 100% purchase would be needed for $60,000, and at the measured 18% about 833 reachable ranges would be needed in total - worth stating so the research step's bar is clear.
